features: DATABASE CHANGE — Four new columns on subentri (annullato_il, annullato_da, nota_annullamento, registro), with a re-runnable migration and no data backfill. One topic only: cancelling a title-transfer record that was entered by mistake.

THE PROBLEM — Until now a recorded transfer could not be cancelled. With the wrong deed date, or the wrong person, it was corrected by hand: rows were closed, associations redone, and the instalments passed to the new owner and the settlement stayed wherever the transfer had put them.

FROM THE HISTORY, THE LAST TRANSFER, WITH INSTALMENTS UNTOUCHED — In the unit's history («Who has owned this unit»), under the transfer, there is «Cancel the transfer…». Before confirming it states only what that transfer actually changed — the ownership rows it wrote, the instalments passed to the new owner, with the same rules as before, the settlement — and what is left to do; a note is required. Only the unit's last transfer can be cancelled, together with any attachments passed along with it.

WHEN THE COMMAND IS NOT THERE — A transfer is cancelled only if, after it, it has no issued instalments, payments (even from another owner) or unverified portal-reported payments on a quota the cancellation would change, if none of its rows was corrected by hand, if a row associated by hand afterwards does not clash with the one that would return, and if the settlement is not already inside a plan. Otherwise «why?» says what to sort out first: the issued instalments, plan by plan, with the full path if payments already exist; the settlement to cancel first, when cancelling the issuance asks for it; the transfer that comes after, and which history it is cancelled from; the conflicting row, with the right path depending on whether it was associated afterwards or corrected from before.

THE CANCELLED TRANSFER STAYS — In the history, with the date, who cancelled it and the note; no calculation reads it anymore: not the allocation, not the joint-liability note, not the charges statement. It stays even on a unit the cancellation leaves without owners. A person entered by mistake can be deleted, and the history still names them from its record.

THE RECORD — From this version every transfer writes down what it did — rows closed, opened and changed, instalments moved — and cancelling it reads that back in reverse, recognising instalments not by id alone but by the trace the transfer leaves inside each one (KondoManager states MySQL 5.7+, and on MySQL 5.7 a restart can make a new instalment reuse the id of one that vanished with its plan). Transfers recorded before this version have no record: they cannot be cancelled, and the program says so; they are corrected by hand, from «Edit association» and «Associate person», as before.

WHEN CANCELLING IS NOT ENOUGH BY ITSELF — A plan generated or recalculated after the transfer, not yet issued, with instalments the cancellation would change — for the person who entered, the person who left, or whoever took over the days left uncovered — does not block anything: the cancellation warns that it needs recalculating, with a message that stays on the page until you close it. A plan recalculated or deleted that had already taken away the transfer's draft instalments does not block anything either: there is nothing left to put back.

CONCURRENT WRITES — Cancelling a transfer, recording one on the same unit, issuing instalments, generating a plan and «Associate person» / «Edit association» no longer overwrite one another: they queue up. Issuance charges whoever holds the instalment at the moment it is issued; a portal report in flight waits and then reads the current state; a plan that was using a balance removed in the meantime stops instead of generating instalments against a number that no longer exists.

ALSO FIXED — Two messages said a recorded transfer «cannot be cancelled (coming in the next version)»: it can now be cancelled from the history, and they say so. In the history, the recording date and the cancellation date were the server's: between midnight and two a.m. in Rome they showed the day before. The reminder counter in the agenda stayed stale for ten minutes after a cancellation.

THE LIMITS — A transfer in the middle of a chain cannot be cancelled, nor one with instalments issued to the person who entered: the one after it, or the issuance, must be cancelled first, with the full path if payments already exist. The document attached to the transfer stays in the unit's archive. Sale with reserved usufruct arrives with beta.38.
